sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module setup and core tables
sections.what: Sets the batch size for saving to 5,000 and lists the four core tables: project, work breakdown, tasks and task links. How this list is used is not shown in this part.
sections.why: Primavera XER exports are built from these table names.

sections.name: _first
sections.title: Picking the first filled field
sections.what: Returns the first non-blank value from a list of field names, so one of several possible spellings can be used.
sections.why: Likely reason: XER exports from different P6 versions name fields differently.

sections.name: _date
sections.title: Converting a date with its location
sections.what: Passes a date value through the shared date conversion and tags any warning with the table and row.
sections.why: XER date problems get the same handling as other formats.

sections.name: ingest_xer (part 1)
sections.title: Reading the file line by line
sections.what: Fingerprints the file and reads each line, tracking the current table and its column names. It stops at the end marker and stops early when cancelled. A row too wide for the limit stops the file with an error. Rows placed before their column names are flagged as errors.
sections.why: A table's column names must be known before its values can be read.
sections.watch_out: Rows that appear before their column names are flagged as errors, and their values cannot be read.

summary: Reads Primavera P6 XER export files, which are plain text made of named tables, and stores their rows.
purpose: Lets users bring in Primavera schedules directly, with projects, work breakdown, tasks and task links.
why: XER files are a sequence of table blocks, so the reader must learn each table's column names before it can read its rows. Only part of the reader is visible in the packet, so the full reason for the remaining logic cannot be stated here.
how: It fingerprints the file, then reads it line by line. A table marker starts a block, a field marker gives the column names, and a record marker introduces a row. An end marker stops reading. Dates and numbers are converted with the shared helpers. Only the first part of the logic is visible, so the rest is not described here.
inputs: A Primavera XER text file and optional progress and cancel callbacks.
outputs: A staging database with the parsed records and an ingestion report. The full output is not visible in the packet.
risks: A record with too many columns stops the file. Records that appear before their column names are flagged as errors. The remaining logic is not in the packet, so its risks cannot be assessed.
debug: If an XER file fails, check the marker lines in the file, especially whether the column names come before the records. Check the warnings for records that appear before a column declaration.
